entries.subject: account
entries.label: Open cases right now
entries.sentence: The number of cases open right now changed
entries.help: Counts the cases that are open at this moment, the same way the rest of the product counts them, and compares it with the last count. Say "surpassed 40", "dropped below 5", or just "changed" to fire on any move. A crossing fires ONLY on the count that crosses, so an account sitting above the bar does not re-trigger. This is NOT the same as cases OPENED recently: an account that opened three cases last week and closed all three has none open now.

openCases.label: Open cases now
openCases.help: The value it changed TO. Empty on the first count we ever take for an account: a crossing needs a before as well as an after.

openCasesChange.label: Change since the previous count
openCasesChange.help: Positive when the backlog grew, negative when it shrank, so "is over 5" is a jump and "is under -5" is a clear-out.

samplingGapDays.label: Days since the previous count
samplingGapDays.help: Normally 1. A larger gap means the counts either side of it are further apart than a day, so the change happened somewhere inside it.

entries.subject: account
entries.label: Cases opened in a period
entries.sentence: The number of cases opened during the chosen period changed
entries.help: Counts how many cases were OPENED inside a rolling period ending now -- the last week (7 days), month (30 days) or quarter (90 days). Pick the period first, then say "is over 5", "is under 2", "surpassed 5" or just "changed". This counts cases STARTING, not cases still open: an account that opened three last week and closed all three still counts three. A period reaching back further than we have been watching an account is not counted at all rather than counted short, so nothing fires for it. As an EXIT, the period you pick is how fast it can close: a quarter-scoped exit answers more slowly than a week-scoped one.

window.label: Period
window.help: Which period the count is over. Required -- a play that does not say would fire on all three.

casesOpened.label: Cases opened in the period
casesOpened.help: The value it changed TO. This count moves when a case is opened AND when an older one falls out of the far end of the period, because the period always ends now.

casesOpenedChange.label: Change since the previous count
casesOpenedChange.help: Positive when intake rose, negative when it fell.

windowDays.label: Days in the period
windowDays.help: How many days the period covers: 7, 30 or 90.

entries.subject: account
entries.label: ARR changed
entries.sentence: The ARR changed
entries.help: Fires on a change to the account's annual recurring revenue in Salesforce. Say "changed by more than 10%", "surpassed 100000", or just "changed" to fire on any move. A change with either side missing is not a change: it means we could not read the figure, and nothing fires.

arr.label: ARR now
arr.help: The value it changed TO. A crossing fires ONLY on the change that crosses -- an account that stays above the bar does not re-trigger.

changePercent.label: Change since the previous value (%)
changePercent.help: Positive is growth, negative is a fall, so "is over 10" is expansion and "is under -10" is contraction. This is the move from the value immediately before it, NOT the comparison with last year -- that one is the "ARR change vs last year" filter. Empty when the previous value was zero, because a percentage of nothing has no meaning.

entries.subject: account

entries.help: The pure change event. Add a condition to say WHICH field, and what it changed to -- "Health status (Salesforce) changed to Red". Covers every mapped Account field as well as the built-in ones.

newValue.label: Changed to
newValue.help: The value it changed TO, compared as text -- "Red", "true". Numeric comparisons such as "greater than" are not available on this field yet.

oldValue.label: Changed from
oldValue.help: The value it changed FROM, as text.

table.label: Source table
table.help: Which table the change was recorded against.

entries.help: The pure change event, on a contact rather than the account. Add a condition to say WHICH field, and what it changed to. Fans out per contact: two contacts changing produce two playbooks.

field.label: Field
field.help: Which tracked contact field changed. Required.

newValue.label: Changed to
newValue.help: The value it changed TO, compared as text -- "true", "Director". Numeric comparisons such as "greater than" are not available on this field yet.

oldValue.label: Changed from
oldValue.help: The value it changed FROM, as text.

table.label: Source table
table.help: Which table the change was recorded against.

contactName.label: Contact name
contactName.help: As entered in Salesforce. May be blank if only an email is held.

entries.subject: contact
entries.label: Contact removed from the account
entries.sentence: A contact was removed from Salesforce
entries.help: Fires when a contact we had synced is no longer returned by Salesforce -- deleted, or moved out of the portfolio. Fans out per contact. Covers EVERY contact; narrow on "Was the key operational contact" for champions only, or use Champion departed, which also catches the three routes that leave the contact in place.

wasKeyOperationalContact.label: Was the key operational contact
wasKeyOperationalContact.help: Whether the person held the Key Operational Contact checkbox when they were last synced. Blank for a removal recorded before this was captured -- the contact row is gone, so it cannot be backfilled.

entries.subject: account
entries.label: Health reading changed
entries.sentence: A new health reading came in
entries.help: The COLOUR half of a new reading -- "changed to Red", "went to Amber or Red from anything else", or simply "the colour changed". For the score, use "Health score changed"; for a sustained slide rather than a single reading, "Health score dropped over a period".

color.label: Changed to — our agent's colour
color.help: The health agent's own colour, not the Salesforce status.

prevColor.label: Changed from — our agent's colour
prevColor.help: Null on an account's first ever reading, and that case still fires: "changed to" already requires the previous colour to be different, so you do not need a second row saying so. Narrow here only when the transition itself matters — "to Red, and only from Green".

samplingGapDays.label: Days since the previous reading
samplingGapDays.help: Readings are only written when an account changes, so a large gap means this comparison is against stale evidence.

entries.subject: account
entries.label: Health score changed
entries.sentence: The health score changed
entries.help: One reading's score compared with the one before it. Say "dropped below 40", "surpassed 70", or just "changed" to fire on any move. A crossing fires ONLY on the reading that crosses -- an account that stays below 40 does not re-trigger.

score.label: Score now
score.help: Null previous score means this is the account's first ever reading, and nothing crossed or changed: a crossing needs a before as well as an after.

samplingGapDays.label: Days since the previous reading
samplingGapDays.help: Readings are only written when an account changes, so a large gap means this comparison is against stale evidence.

entries.subject: user
entries.label: New user in the customer org
entries.sentence: A new user was created in the customer org
entries.help: Read from the customer's own Salesforce, once a day. Fans out per user: five new users produce five playbooks. Counts staff logins only -- not portal, guest or automated accounts. A user created before we started reading that org does not fire.

profileName.label: Profile
profileName.help: Salesforce's permission profile, e.g. System Administrator.

userRoleName.label: Role
userRoleName.help: Position in the org's role hierarchy. Often blank.

entries.subject: user
entries.label: User deactivated in the customer org
entries.sentence: A user was deactivated in the customer org
entries.help: Salesforce does not allow deleting a user, so leaving is recorded as deactivation -- that is what this reads. Fans out per user. A user who simply stops appearing is NOT counted: that cannot be told apart from a permission change on our side.

tenureDays.label: Days they were a user
tenureDays.help: From their Salesforce creation date to the deactivation. A three-week tenure and a nine-year one are different conversations.

entries.subject: user
entries.label: User changed role in the customer org
entries.sentence: A user's role or permission profile changed in the customer org
entries.help: Covers both the Salesforce role and the permission profile. One playbook per person per day, however many of the two moved. Narrow it with "Only when..." if you want profile changes but not role changes.

changeKind.label: What changed
changeKind.help: The profile decides what someone can do; the role decides what they can see through the hierarchy.

entries.subject: account
entries.label: A metric changed period over period
entries.sentence: An account metric changed from one period to the one before it
entries.help: Compares a metric with itself one period earlier: last month against the month before, or last quarter against the quarter before. Say which metric and which comparison, then say "changePercent is under -20" for a 20% fall, "change is under -5000" for a fall in amount, or "value changed" to fire on any move. Negative is a fall and positive is a rise, on both. THE QUARTER IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR EVERY METRIC: we have no quarterly figures, so a quarter is built from its three months, and how to build it depends on what the metric counts -- donations add up, a membership count does not (three months of members is the same members three times, so its quarter is where it ENDED). Where that has not been established for a metric we offer the month comparison only, rather than guess. If either period is missing we say NOTHING rather than reporting a change of zero: with only one period there is no comparison to make. As an EXIT this is a slow one: a comparison arrives once a period, so a play closing on the month pair closes at the start of a month and one closing on the quarter pair four times a year.

metricCode.label: Metric
metricCode.help: Which metric. Only metrics we can actually compare are listed -- one with a single period of data has nothing to compare against.

periodPair.label: Comparison
periodPair.help: Which two periods. Required -- a play that does not say would fire once for the month comparison and again for the quarter on the same news.

value.label: Value this period
value.help: The value it moved TO. Declaring the value before is what makes "surpassed", "dropped below" and "changed" available here.

change.label: Change in amount
change.help: This period minus the one before, in the metric's own units. Negative is a fall, so "is under -5000" is a drop of five thousand or more. Always present -- including when the previous period was zero, where there is no percentage but the amount is perfectly real.

changePercent.label: Change in percentage
changePercent.help: The same move as a percentage of the earlier period. Negative is a fall, so "is under -20" is the product's "dropped by 20%". Empty when the earlier period was zero, because a percentage of nothing has no meaning -- use the amount instead.
